text:
Marathon Petroleum fell nearly 11% over the past two weeks, with most of that damage occurring between November 3rd and 6th. The primary driver has been a sharp drop in oil prices: Brent crude slipped below $90 a barrel on November 10th — the lowest since August — after President Trump signaled the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon," easing geopolitical risk. Refiners like Marathon profit when the gap between crude oil costs and refined product prices widens; when oil prices fall this sharply, that margin often compresses, weighing on earnings.

The stock has stabilized over the past few days even as oil prices continued falling, suggesting the market may be pricing in some adjustment to a lower oil regime. Refineries are running at a healthy 94.5% capacity, and storage levels for gasoline and diesel remain moderate, so there's no supply crunch offsetting the crude price decline — the headwind is purely from lower input costs squeezing refiner margins.
